question.text: Which of the following is an unsecured form of borrowing?

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 72 of the workbook defines unsecured loans and gives personal loans and credit card dues as examples. Pages 77-78 add that personal loans have no security and are more expensive than asset-backed loans, while loans against securities, gold, or property are secured. The Trap: Home loans, gold loans, and loans against mutual fund units are all secured by a specific asset (mortgage, pledge, or lien), so they are not unsecured. Note: Because there is no asset backing, unsecured loans typically carry a higher interest rate than equivalent secured products such as loans against securities or gold.
